name: @appstrate/expo-mcp
description: Expo integration backed by Expo's hosted remote MCP server (mcp.expo.dev/mcp): EAS builds and submissions, EAS Workflows, TestFlight crashes and feedback, Play Console crashes, App Store and Play Store reviews and replies, and the Expo documentation. The sidecar opens a Streamable HTTP MCP client and injects the actor's OAuth2 access token as `Authorization: Bearer …`. Authorization is fully standards-based, so no OAuth app is registered by hand: RFC 9728 protected-resource discovery on /mcp, RFC 8414 authorization-server metadata on the mcp.expo.dev issuer, RFC 7591 Dynamic Client Registration as a public client (`token_endpoint_auth_method: none`) and RFC 7636 PKCE (S256); the operator installs the connector and each member clicks Connect. The single `mcp:access` scope covers every tool, the Expo account's own permissions bound what each one can reach, and the authorization server offers no offline scope or authorize parameter to ask for a refresh token (`refresh_token_issuance: "default"`). There is no userinfo endpoint, so connections are told apart by the issuer alone. Phase 4 (per-tool URL envelope) is N/A — every tool transits the same /mcp endpoint. `search_documentation` needs a paid EAS plan upstream. Expo's local capabilities (simulator automation, app logs, devtools, router sitemap) need the `expo-mcp` dev dependency and a local dev server, so they are out of reach of a sandboxed run and not declared here.
